batch_note: Two cross-item patterns. (1) Construction template: nearly every passage gives each distractor one dedicated refuting clause, often an oddly specific or trailing detail that seems irrelevant to the main point (A-01 'thirty miles off', B-07 'no chairs', C-01 'Both rows' aphids multiplied', C-05 'gale took no stone', D-04 'lawns slope open to the highway', D-06 memoirs line, E-04 'ditches draw on springs', E-07 'freighters draw twenty'). A solver who learns that each odd detail kills exactly one option can find the key as the only option left unrefuted without understanding the passage's logic. This applies to roughly all 40 items. (2) The stock or textbook metaphor/collocation is the trap, not the key, in A-02 (corridor), B-02 (reduced), C-01 (herded), C-04 (depository), D-02 (kidney), D-04 (magnet), E-02 (winnowed), E-04 (thermometer) and E-08 (vault). 'Avoid the cliche' does not predict every key (A-07 capsized, B-07 pawnshop and B-08 rutted are the expected word), so the tell is partial. Surface template: 'the report/historian concluded that the X had ______ the Y', ending in a trailing filler sentence, recurs across C-01, C-05 to C-08, D-01, D-06 to D-08, E-02, E-05 and E-06. Options in each set share initial letters (A set b/c, B set p/r, C set d to g, D set i to n, E set s to w), which is cosmetic and does not predict the key. Key letters are balanced at 10/10/10/10.
